prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofing company that fits every homeowner — the best choice depends on your budget, roof type, timeline, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and your location in the Dallas metro area. I can help you find the right one. To start, tell me your ZIP code and any priorities (price, longest warranty, fastest start, insurance help, brand certification, etc.). 

While you decide, use this checklist to evaluate and compare Dallas roofers:

Must-check items
- License & insurance: verify contractor liability insurance and workers’ comp (get certificate of insurance). Ask for license/registration numbers and confirm they’re current.
- Local experience & references: request recent local job references and photos. Check Google/Yelp/BBB reviews.
- Manufacturer certifications: look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, or similar (these give extended warranties).
- Written estimate & contract: get a detailed written estimate showing materials, brand/model of shingles, underlayment, ventilation, flashing, permits, cleanup, and timeline.
- Warranties: confirm both manufacturer (shingle) and workmanship/installation warranty in writing, and learn how claims are handled.
- Permits & code compliance: contractor should pull required permits and handle inspections.
- Payment terms: avoid large upfront payments (typical schedule: small deposit, progress payments, final on completion). Get lien waivers.
- Disposal & cleanup: confirm how old roofing will be removed and hauled away and how they will protect landscaping.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you registered/licensed in Texas and insured? Can I see proof?
- Are you a certified installer by any shingle manufacturers?
- Who will be my project manager/crew foreman and how long have you been in business locally?
- Will you pull permits and meet city code?
- What underlayment, flashing, vents, ice/water barrier (if applicable) will you install?
- What is your warranty (length and what it covers)? How are warranty claims handled?
- Do you provide a written contract and final inspection report?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately or to use a single insurer/adjuster.
- No physical address or only a cell phone number.
- Mostly 1-star reviews or many unresolved BBB complaints.
- Very low bid compared to others (could be cutting corners or bait).

If you share your ZIP code (or address) and what matters most to you, I’ll put together 3–5 well-vetted Dallas-area roofers to contact and can include which questions to ask each and what to compare in their bids.
